The producer fix is therefore working and this drains by 09-22 with no intervention. What is NOT fixed in-repo is the RELEASE side: packs/scheduling/lib/tasks/scheduled_posting.rake publishes EVERY due post in one run (no per-day cap, no minimum spacing), and bin/scheduled_posting.sh runs hourly from the user crontab (0 * * * *), so 314+327 release together at the 05:00Z tick and 334+335 together at 17:00Z -- that is the 09-19 04:38-06:00Z four-in-90min burst (posted_24h=4, all of them). Two candidate fixes, both Tim's call because they change public posting behaviour: (a) enforce growth max_posts_per_day in the publisher, or (b) release at most one due post per tick. I did NOT change the publisher: a defect there stalls publishing silently, which is the worst failure class on this board. Do not close this by re-spacing rows -- the rows are fine, the releaser is the mechanism.

2026-09-20 05:4xZ ops-triage: the RELEASE side is now fixed (commit a201900) -- Scheduling::PostReleasePlan makes scheduled_posting.rake release at most ONE post per run, so bunched slots no longer leave the account as a burst. Verified end-to-end with a rake spec (2 due -> 1 posted, 1 still 'scheduled', posted_at nil) and the full suite 383/0. No row edits: the rows are the producer's output, the burst was the releaser's.
